Using the SEBI Master Circulars for Investment Advisers and Research Analysts dated 6 February 2026, assess this plan for a partnership firm registered as both an IA and an RA. Its peak client counts in the previous financial year were 280 advisory clients and 425 research clients; it currently has only 120 clients in each business. For an ordinary, non-accredited individual client family, it proposes fixed annual fees of Rs 160,000 for investment advice and Rs 160,000 for research, excluding statutory charges. It wants to collect 18 months of fees upfront and retain three months of fees if either contract is terminated early. It also wants to operate advisory and research as one undifferentiated service. Explain: (1) the dual-registration compliance and segregation requirements; (2) the annual fee ceiling and maximum advance period for each service; (3) how refunds and breakage fees differ between IA and RA; (4) the deposit required for each registration, the lien beneficiary, which client counts determine the deposit, and the deadline for updating it; and (5) which fee rules change for corporate clients or accredited investors. Cite both circulars and distinguish their rules.
notes: Compare both roles, apply prior-year peaks, retain required undertaking, and disclose main-rule/MITC advance-fee discrepancy.

question: Using SEBI's 6 Feb 2026 Master Circulars for Investment Advisers (IA) and Research Analysts (RA): a dual-registered partnership had prior-year peak counts of 280 IA clients and 425 RA clients, now 120 each. For non-accredited individual families it proposes Rs 160,000/year per service (excluding statutory charges), 18 months' advance, three months' fee retained on early termination, and undifferentiated IA/RA activities. Assess separately for IA and RA: dual-registration/segregation duties; annual fee ceiling; allowed advance; unexpired-fee refunds and breakage; required deposit, lien body, client-count basis and adjustment deadline. Explain fee exceptions for corporate clients and accredited investors. Cite both circulars.
